title: Scenario catalog generator and publisher for benchmark profile artifacts
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a reusable generator that emits a 'scenario catalog' used by the benchmark harness to produce model performance profiles. The catalog will encode dataset slices, prompt template variants, evaluation runner configuration, and metadata needed for reproducible profile generation and model version pinning. Deliverables: CLI + library to generate catalogs, schema validator, integration tests with eval runners, and an automated publisher that writes profile artifacts to the profile registry with model version references.
background: Onboarding new model variants today requires one-off scripts to shape datasets and prompts; that causes subtle drift in eval runs and inconsistent profiles. We need a canonical artifact (scenario catalog) that captures intent (slices / prompts / runner flags), deterministic sampling seeds, and the model pins used to generate a profile so downstream consumers (Console, Optimize, Dedicated) can reason about regressions and rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Catalog generator emits JSON catalog that conforms to the profile-catalog schema v1 and passes schema validation
Eval harness consumes catalog to run deterministic evals and produces a matching profile artifact with model version pin metadata
CI job verifies generation + one sample eval end-to-end and stores generated profile in the profile-registry bucket
CLI supports two modes: sampled (fast, n=500 per scenario) and exhaustive (configurable combinatorial expansion), documented in README
Automated publisher attaches tags: model_name, model_version, catalog_id, git_sha and returns an immutable artifact URL
technical_approach: Implement generator as a small Python package used by onboarding engineers and the harness. Key components: 1) catalog schema and validator (jsonschema), 2) prompt templating layer with variant folding and guardrails for token length, 3) deterministic sampler with configurable RNG seed and stratified sampling policy, 4) runner descriptor that maps to harness adapter names and per-scenario runner flags, 5) publisher that uploads to profile-registry and writes provenance metadata for version pinning.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Full combinatorial expansion can produce very large catalogs; default to sampled mode in CI and allow exhaustive runs in nightly or release pipelines
Store prompt variants inline in catalog to keep artifacts self-contained; accept larger artifact size in exchange for reproducibility
Use jsonschema v7 for widest compatibility across our infra agents rather than the newer $defs-only formats
Expose a compact CSV export for quick manual inspection in Console and for non-JSON consumers
